contracao-de-pico.name: Peak Contraction
contracao-de-pico.summary: Hold 1-2s at the point of peak contraction on every rep, squeezing before you release.

sections.what: A short, active pause at the point where the muscle is most shortened.
sections.how: Lift normally, hold 1-2 seconds squeezing the target muscle, then lower under control.
sections.when: Isolation work and machines, where you can clearly feel the target.
sections.mistake: Pausing with your body instead of the muscle. If you lock the joint and rest, the technique is gone.

piramide-crescente.name: Ascending Pyramid
piramide-crescente.summary: Add weight and drop reps on every set. Start light, finish heavy.

sections.what: Load climbs set by set while reps come down.
sections.how: Example: 15 reps → 12 → 10 → 8, adding weight each time. The last set is the heaviest.
sections.when: On the first exercise of a muscle group, to warm into heavy work safely.
sections.mistake: Adding weight too early and arriving empty on the set that actually mattered.

falha-concentrica.name: Concentric Failure
falha-concentrica.summary: Rep out until you can no longer lift the weight on your own. Stop when the lift fails.

sections.what: The point where you cannot complete another lift with good form.
sections.how: Go until the rep stalls on the way up. That is the end of the set — do not force it with momentum.
sections.when: On the last set of an exercise, or when the plan calls for it explicitly.
sections.mistake: Confusing failure with discomfort. Failure is mechanical: the weight stops moving.

no-reps.name: No Reps
no-reps.summary: No fixed rep target. Do what you can with good form, within the prescribed effort.

sections.what: The plan sets sides and rest but leaves the rep count open.
sections.how: Work to the effort the set asks for, usually close to failure, without counting a target.
sections.when: When the goal is effort rather than an exact volume.
sections.mistake: Treating it as "do whatever you feel like". The stopping rule still exists — it just is not a number.

drop-set.name: Drop Set
drop-set.summary: Reach failure, strip 20-30% of the weight immediately, and keep going with no rest.

sections.what: An extension of the set: you shed load and keep going, with no pause.
sections.how: Hit failure, cut roughly 20-30% of the weight within seconds, and keep going until you fail again.
sections.when: On the last set of an exercise. Machines and cables are the most practical.
sections.mistake: Taking too long to change the weight — over ~10 seconds it becomes a new set, not a drop.

1-rest.name: 1 Rest
1-rest.summary: Rest-pause with a single round: hit failure, rest ~15s, do one more block at the same weight.

sections.what: Rest-pause run once instead of the usual three rounds.
sections.how: Go to failure. Rest about 15 seconds without leaving position. Do one more block at the same weight.
sections.when: When the plan wants rest-pause intensity without the recovery cost of three rounds.
sections.mistake: Stretching the pause. Past ~20 seconds it stopped being a rest-pause and became a new set.

repeticoes-de-reserva.name: Reps in Reserve
repeticoes-de-reserva.summary: Stop with 1-3 reps still in the tank. Do not go to failure.

sections.what: A deliberate brake: you end the set before failure.
sections.how: If you finished feeling you had two more in you, you left two in reserve. That is the target.
sections.when: On most sets of a volume session, to accumulate work without emptying the tank.
sections.mistake: Overestimating the reserve. Most people are closer to failure than they think.

cluster.name: Cluster Set
cluster.summary: Break the set into short blocks with 10-20s pauses between them, keeping the load heavy.

sections.what: A set broken into mini-blocks with planned micro-rests.
sections.how: Example: 3 reps, 15s pause, 3 reps, 15s, 3 reps. It counts as a single set.
sections.when: When you want volume at heavy loads without losing execution.
sections.mistake: Letting the pauses stretch until it becomes three ordinary sets.

no-stop.name: No-Stop
no-stop.summary: No pause between reps and no rest until the set is done. Continuous movement.

sections.what: Continuous tension: the muscle never rests at any point of the movement.
sections.how: Do not lock out at the top or relax at the bottom. Up and down without stopping.
sections.when: Isolation, machines and finishers. Very common on glutes, calves and abs.
sections.mistake: Cutting the range short to keep the rhythm going.

rest-pause.name: Rest-Pause
rest-pause.summary: Go to failure, rest 10-20s, resume at the same weight. Repeat 2-3 times.

sections.what: Several rounds of failure separated by very short pauses, without changing the weight.
sections.how: Failure → 10-20s → more reps to failure → 10-20s → final round.
sections.when: Last set of an exercise, when you want intensity without adding load.
sections.mistake: Turning the short pause into a full rest, which just makes it three separate sets.

tensao-progressiva.name: Progressive Tension
tensao-progressiva.summary: Raise the demand each set - load, time under tension, or range - without losing form.

sections.what: Progression inside the session itself: each set demands slightly more than the last.
sections.how: The rising variable can be weight, tempo or range. The plan or your coach decides which.
sections.when: When you want a rising stimulus without hitting failure on the very first set.
sections.mistake: Raising the demand and dropping technique along with it.

3-a-7.name: 3/7 Method
3-a-7.summary: Five blocks of 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 reps with ~15s rest between them, same weight throughout.

sections.what: A ladder of ascending blocks with very short rests, counted as one exercise.
sections.how: 3 reps → 15s → 4 → 15s → 5 → 15s → 6 → 15s → 7. Same weight from start to finish.
sections.when: When you want high fatigue accumulation with a moderate load.
sections.mistake: Picking a weight that is too heavy and failing to finish the last blocks.

excentrica-lenta.name: Slow Eccentric
excentrica-lenta.summary: Lower the weight slowly (3-5s) and lift at normal speed. The descent is what counts.

sections.what: Emphasis on the phase where the muscle lengthens under load.
sections.how: Count 3 to 5 seconds on the way down. The lift back up is normal and controlled.
sections.when: When you want a strong stimulus without heavy load, or to clean up movement control.
sections.mistake: Counting too fast. Time it for the first few sessions.

strip-set.name: Strip Set
strip-set.summary: Several drops back to back: fail, strip, fail again, strip again, until the weight runs out.

sections.what: A chained drop set, with three or more reductions back to back.
sections.how: Failed? Strip weight, keep going. Repeat until the load is minimal. No rest between changes.
sections.when: As a finisher for a muscle group. Works best on cables, machines or dumbbells on a rack.
sections.mistake: Choosing an exercise where you cannot change the weight quickly.

oclusao.name: Blood Flow Restriction
oclusao.summary: Training with partial blood flow restriction, light load and high reps.
oclusao.caution: Requires in-person guidance from a professional to set cuff pressure and duration. Do not improvise with generic bands.

sections.what: Using a cuff or band high on the limb to partially restrict venous return during light sets.
sections.how: Light load (typically 20-30% of max), high reps, short rest, cuff applied as instructed.
sections.when: When you want a stimulus with very little load.
sections.mistake: Over-tightening the cuff or leaving it on for too long.

bi-set.name: Superset
bi-set.summary: Two exercises back to back with no rest between them. Rest comes only after the pair.

sections.what: A pair of exercises treated as one unit of training.
sections.how: Finish the first and move straight into the second. Rest starts only after both.
sections.when: To save time, raise density, or pair muscles that do not compete with each other.
sections.mistake: Picking two stations far apart — the walk becomes the rest that was not supposed to exist.

repeticoes-rapidas.name: Fast Reps
repeticoes-rapidas.summary: Accelerated tempo with control. Focus on speed, not maximum load.

sections.what: A fast cadence while keeping range and control.
sections.how: Lift with the intent to move fast and lower without throwing the weight. Full range still applies.
sections.when: Finishers and power work with light to moderate loads.
sections.mistake: Trading speed for swing — if the body helps, the muscle is no longer working.

m-tut.name: M-TUT
m-tut.summary: Extended time under tension: every rep is slow in both phases, with no lockout.

sections.what: Maximizing the total time the muscle spends under load within the set.
sections.how: Controlled, slow on the way up and on the way down, with no pause at the top or bottom.
sections.when: Isolation and machines, where continuous tension is safe to hold.
sections.mistake: Locking out at the top, which hands the load to the joint and ends the tension.

falha-total.name: Total Failure
falha-total.summary: Go until you cannot move the weight in any direction, not even control the descent.
falha-total.caution: Do not use on free-weight movements with the load over your body or head without a spotter and safety pins.

sections.what: The point beyond concentric failure, where even a controlled descent is impossible.
sections.how: Only on exercises where dropping the weight is safe — machine, cable, or with a partner.
sections.when: Rarely, and on the last set. It is very expensive in recovery terms.
sections.mistake: Using it on a free-weight lift with the bar over your body.

fst-7.name: FST-7
fst-7.summary: Seven sets of the last exercise for the muscle, 30-45s rest, chasing maximum pump.

sections.what: A seven-set finisher on the isolation movement that closes a muscle group.
sections.how: 7 sets, 8-12 reps, 30-45 seconds rest, moderate load.
sections.when: As the last exercise for a muscle group, never at the start.
sections.mistake: Picking a load that is too heavy and failing to hold up across all seven sets.

forca-pura.name: Pure Strength
forca-pura.summary: Heavy loads and low reps with long rest. Focus on strength, not volume.

sections.what: A heavy working range, typically 1 to 5 reps, with generous rest between sets.
sections.how: Warm up progressively first. Rest long enough that the next set is as good as the last.
sections.when: On the compound lifts that open the session.
sections.mistake: Cutting the rest short and turning it into endurance work with a heavy weight.

apneia.name: Breath Hold
apneia.summary: Hold your breath through a short stretch of the movement to raise intra-abdominal pressure.
apneia.caution: Can cause dizziness and raise blood pressure. Anyone with a cardiovascular condition, hypertension, or who is pregnant should consult a professional first.

sections.what: Holding air through the hardest part of the rep, stabilising the trunk.
sections.how: Breathe in before, hold through the demanding stretch, exhale on completion. Short stretches only.
sections.when: Lifts that need a rigid trunk, and specific core work.
sections.mistake: Holding your breath across entire sets in a row.

slow.name: Slow
slow.summary: Slow movement in both phases, no momentum and no pause, holding constant tension.

sections.what: A reduced cadence from the beginning to the end of the repetition.
sections.how: No swing, no lockout. The load has to be lighter than usual.
sections.when: Learning a movement, or when there is not enough load available.
sections.mistake: Speeding up as fatigue sets in, which quietly turns it back into a normal set.

aquecimento.name: Warm-Up
aquecimento.summary: Light sets before the working sets, to prepare the joint and the movement pattern.

sections.what: Specific preparation for the exercise that follows.
sections.how: 1 to 3 sets well below working weight, never taken near effort.
sections.when: Before the first heavy movement of each muscle group.
sections.mistake: Making it hard enough to count as a working set, which just eats into the real ones.

explosao-concentrica.name: Concentric Explosion
explosao-concentrica.summary: Lift with maximum intent to accelerate and lower under control.

sections.what: Emphasis on the intent to accelerate during the lifting phase.
sections.how: Push or pull as fast as you can; lower at a normal, controlled speed.
sections.when: Compound movements at moderate loads.
sections.mistake: Letting the descent become a free fall — only the lift is fast.

piramide-decrescente.name: Descending Pyramid
piramide-decrescente.summary: Drop weight and add reps on every set. Start heavy.

sections.what: The reverse of the ascending pyramid: the heaviest set comes first.
sections.how: Example: 6 reps → 8 → 10 → 12, stripping weight each time.
sections.when: When you want to attack the heavy set fresh, with warm-up done separately.
sections.mistake: Skipping the warm-up and going straight into the heaviest set.

piramidal.name: Pyramid
piramidal.summary: Load and reps vary across sets instead of staying fixed. Can be ascending or descending.

sections.what: The generic term. The plan says pyramid without naming a direction.
sections.how: If it is not specified, the common default is ascending: more weight, fewer reps each set.
sections.when: Whenever the plan names the technique without a direction.
sections.mistake: Assuming the direction rather than checking. Ascending and descending train different things.

tri-set.name: Tri-Set
tri-set.summary: Three exercises back to back with no rest. Rest comes only after all three.

sections.what: Like a bi-set, but with three exercises in the block.
sections.how: Chain all three and rest only after the last one.
sections.when: High density and time savings. Usually closes a muscle group.
sections.mistake: Building it from three stations that are far apart, or usually occupied.

carga-progressiva.name: Progressive Overload
carga-progressiva.summary: Increase the load across weeks as you reach the top of the rep range.

sections.what: The principle of progression between sessions, not within one.
sections.how: Hit every set at the top of the rep range with good form? Raise the load next session.
sections.when: It is the default for any strength or hypertrophy plan.
sections.mistake: Raising the load before the reps are actually clean.

isometria.name: Isometric Hold
isometria.summary: Hold the position still, neither lifting nor lowering, for the prescribed time.

sections.what: Contraction with no joint movement.
sections.how: Take the position and hold it for the prescribed time, breathing normally.
sections.when: Core, stabilisers, and as a finisher after a dynamic exercise.
sections.mistake: Holding your breath the whole time.
